questions.prompt: Which of these is an example of a projectile (an object moving under gravity alone)?
options: A rocket with its engine still firing upward
A stone thrown across a river
A car driving along a flat road
A satellite held by ground control thrusters
questions.explanation: A projectile moves under gravity only with no driving force, so a thrown stone qualifies while the others have engines or thrust.

questions.prompt: A ball is kicked at 16 m/s at an angle of 60° above the horizontal. What is its initial vertical velocity component? (sin 60° = 0.866)
questions.explanation: Vertical component = u sin θ = 16 × 0.866 = 13.9 m/s.

questions.prompt: A 0.20 kg ball moves in a horizontal circle of radius 0.40 m at a speed of 6.0 m/s. What centripetal force is needed?
A ball rolls off a horizontal bench 0.80 m high at 2.5 m/s. Using g = 10 m/s², how far from the base of the bench does it land?
questions.explanation: Fall time: 0.80 = ½ × 10 × t² → t² = 0.16 → t = 0.40 s. Horizontal distance = 2.5 × 0.40 = 1.0 m.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched from the ground at 20 m/s at 60° above the horizontal. Using g = 10 m/s² and sin 60° = 0.866, what is the maximum height reached?
A projectile is launched from level ground at 30 m/s at 45° (sin 90° = 1). Using g = 10 m/s², what is its horizontal range?
What is the SI unit of capacitance?
questions.explanation: Capacitance is measured in farads (F), where one farad stores one coulomb per volt.

questions.prompt: A charge of 5.0 × 10⁻⁶ C feels a force of 0.015 N at a point in an electric field. What is the field strength there?
How much charge is stored on a 8.0 µF capacitor connected to a 12 V supply?
questions.explanation: Q = CV = 8.0 µF × 12 V = 96 µC.

questions.prompt: Two equal point charges 0.10 m apart repel with a force of 0.90 N. If the distance is increased to 0.30 m, what is the new force?
questions.explanation: Force follows 1/r². Tripling r divides the force by 3² = 9, so F = 0.90 / 9 = 0.10 N.

questions.prompt: What is the electric field strength 0.20 m from a point charge of 4.0 × 10⁻⁸ C? (Use k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)
Two charges of +2.0 × 10⁻⁶ C and +5.0 × 10⁻⁶ C are placed 0.30 m apart. Using k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N·m²/C², the force between them is closest to:
What is the SI unit of electrical power?
questions.explanation: Electrical power is measured in watts (W), where one watt equals one joule of energy per second.

questions.prompt: A current of 0.25 A flows through a 40 Ω resistor. What is the voltage across it?
questions.explanation: Using Ohm's law V = IR = 0.25 × 40 = 10 V.

questions.prompt: A charge of 90 C flows past a point in a wire in 30 s. What is the current?
questions.explanation: Current I = Q/t = 90 / 30 = 3.0 A.

questions.prompt: Two resistors of 12 Ω and 6.0 Ω are connected in parallel. What is their combined resistance?
An electric iron rated at 1.5 kW operates for 20 minutes. How much electrical energy does it use?
A battery of e.m.f. 6.0 V and internal resistance 0.50 Ω is connected to an external 2.5 Ω resistor. What is the current in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Total resistance = r + R = 0.50 + 2.5 = 3.0 Ω. Current I = ε / (R + r) = 6.0 / 3.0 = 2.0 A.

questions.prompt: What is produced in the region around a permanent magnet?
questions.explanation: A magnet sets up a magnetic field in the space around it, shown by field lines running from north to south outside the magnet.

questions.prompt: A 0.30 m wire carries 4.0 A at right angles to a 0.50 T magnetic field. What is the force on the wire?
Which of the following will produce an induced voltage in a stationary coil of wire?
options: Placing a steady bar magnet inside it
Moving a magnet into or out of the coil
Leaving the coil in a constant field
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic induction needs a changing magnetic field, so moving the magnet relative to the coil induces a voltage.

questions.prompt: A straight wire feels a maximum force of 1.8 N when it carries 6.0 A perpendicular to a 0.60 T field. What is the length of the wire in the field?
A 0.40 m wire carrying 5.0 A is placed parallel to a 0.70 T magnetic field. What force acts on the wire?
questions.explanation: The force F = BIL applies only to the component perpendicular to the field. A wire parallel to the field experiences zero force.

questions.prompt: A wire 0.25 m long carries 8.0 A at right angles to a magnetic field and experiences a force of 0.40 N. What is the magnetic flux density?
Which of the following is the best electrical conductor?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal with many free electrons, so it conducts electricity very well, unlike the insulators listed.

questions.prompt: What are the three doped layers of a transistor called?
questions.explanation: A transistor has three regions named the emitter, base, and collector; a small base current controls a larger collector–emitter current.

questions.prompt: Adding an element such as phosphorus, which has extra valence electrons, to silicon produces which type of semiconductor?
questions.explanation: Extra electrons act as negative charge carriers, so doping with phosphorus produces n-type (negative) semiconductor material.

questions.prompt: A diode is connected so that it blocks the flow of current. In which state is the diode?
questions.explanation: A diode conducts in forward bias and blocks current in reverse bias, so a non-conducting diode is reverse biased.

questions.prompt: A small signal at the base of a transistor controls a much larger collector current of the same shape. Which role is the transistor performing?
questions.explanation: When a small base signal controls a much larger output current of the same shape, the transistor is amplifying the signal.

questions.prompt: What is the main advantage of a transistor over an early vacuum tube that performs the same job?
options: It is larger and easier to see
It is small, reliable, and uses little power
It needs a heated filament to work
It only works at very high voltages
questions.explanation: Transistors replaced vacuum tubes because they are far smaller, more reliable, and consume much less power, with no hot filament needed.

questions.prompt: What is the approximate speed of all electromagnetic waves in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: All electromagnetic waves travel through a vacuum at the speed of light, about 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.prompt: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror with an angle of incidence of 28° measured from the normal. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.explanation: By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, so it is 28°.

questions.prompt: An electromagnetic wave has a wavelength of 2.0 m and travels at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. What is its frequency?
Light travels at 2.4 × 10⁸ m/s inside a transparent plastic. Using c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, what is the refractive index of the plastic?
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = c / v = (3.0 × 10⁸) / (2.4 × 10⁸) = 1.25.

questions.prompt: Light passes from air (n₁ = 1.0) into a glass block (n₂ = 1.5) at an angle of incidence of 30°. Using Snell's law, what is the sine of the angle of refraction? (sin 30° = 0.50)
questions.explanation: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ → sin θ₂ = (1.0 × 0.50) / 1.5 = 0.33.

questions.prompt: A blue light wave has a frequency of 6.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz and travels at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. What is its wavelength?
